claim: Goldstein, Li and Wang (2026-09-03): in Polymarket 2024-01-05..2024-11-05 a one-percentage-point rise in the Trump-win probability goes with 13 bp of next-day return of Trump trades (pooled), and a probability-based strategy shows an annualised Sharpe of 1.95 over April-November 2024; the authors state the statistics are in-sample and gross of transaction costs.
quote: a one-percentage-point increase in Polymarket probability is associated with 13 basis points of next-day returns of Trump trades in the pooled sample.
limitations: Single event, in-sample, gross of costs, no independent replication found; the asset set is election-sensitive ETFs and banks, not individual stocks around announcements.
independent_replication: No independent replication found in the 2026-10-04 search.
impact_on_spec: Mechanism prior only; the earnings design uses within-week ranks, costs and placebos that this paper does not have.

claim: Kalshi distributions are accurate forecasts of macro outcomes (for headline CPI a statistically significant improvement over the Bloomberg consensus); the paper tests forecast accuracy and news response, not stock returns.
quote: for headline CPI, we find Kalshi provides a statistically significant improvement over the Bloomberg consensus forecast.
limitations: Macro releases on Kalshi, not company earnings on Polymarket; accuracy is not the same as tradable alpha after the stock market already prices the information.
independent_replication: Replication code by a third party (WillBtK/macro_kalshi) rebuilds the distributions; no independent replication of the forecast claims found.
impact_on_spec: Context only: justifies treating contract prices as information, and the calibration table as a data sanity check.

claim: SECONDARY (author interview about a companion paper; the earnings paper SSRN 5933475 itself returned HTTP 403): Jensen says that adding the Polymarket earnings contracts to their regression of earnings-announcement surprises made them explain a lot, beyond analyst forecasts.
quote: We added them to the regression almost casually, and suddenly they explained a lot.
limitations: Interview, not the paper; SSRN 5933475 and SSRN papers.cfm pages returned 403 on 2026-10-04 so no coefficient, sample size or standard error was read; the claim is about announcement outcomes, not tradable stock returns net of costs.
independent_replication: None found; the paper is unpublished.
impact_on_spec: Premise only; no number from the paper enters the design.

claim: SECONDARY review of Gomez-Cram, Guo, Jensen and Kung: the market-implied probability classifies 68 percent of announcements correctly seven days ahead and 77 percent one day ahead against 62 percent for analyst forecasts, on a roughly two-month sample; prices lean optimistic in level even when they rank well.
quote: correctly classifies 68 percent of announcements seven days ahead and 77 percent one day ahead, against 62 percent for analyst forecasts issued in the same window.
limitations: Blog review of an unread paper (SSRN 403); numbers are the review's, sample about two months, young market; a 76 percent beat base rate makes 77 percent weak discrimination (see Rabetti et al. card).
independent_replication: Rabetti, Shao and Zhang report a similar hit rate (78.5 percent) on a different sample.
impact_on_spec: Justifies within-week percentile rank (removes the level bias) and the calibration table.

claim: SECONDARY summary (paywalled after the first paragraph; SSRN 6649938 returned 403): Rabetti, Shao and Zhang use 469 Polymarket firm-quarter earnings-beat contracts, analyst forecasts and daily stock prices for September 2025 through February 2026.
quote: Using data for 469 Polymarket firm-quarter earnings beat contracts, corresponding analyst earnings forecast data and associated daily stock prices during September 2025 through February 2026
limitations: Only the first paragraph is public; findings are behind a paywall. No result number is taken from this source.
impact_on_spec: Defines the overlap and post-publication sub-periods (before and from 2026-03-01).

claim: SECONDARY news article on Rabetti, Shao and Zhang: Polymarket bettors called earnings right about 79 percent of the time against 44 percent for analyst consensus, while companies beat 75.9 percent of the time, so always guessing beat looks accurate.
quote: Companies Beat Earnings 75.9% of the Time.
limitations: News article quoting an unread paper; the consensus accuracy is judged on a consensus definition that the article says is biased by walk-downs.
impact_on_spec: Expected-failure item 'prices are noise around a base rate' in hypotheses.md; calibration table reports the sample base rate.

claim: Polymarket Gamma /events with tag earnings and closed=true listed 1354 resolved earnings events on 2026-10-04, each with title containing the ticker, a slug that encodes the consensus EPS and date, an end time and a volume in USD.
limitations: Snapshot omits token ids and outcomes; events may be edited after resolution; Polymarket is an offshore venue and prices are a research input only.
impact_on_spec: Defines event identity fields and the primary-sample volume filter.

claim: The public CLOB /prices-history endpoint returns timestamped prices for a resolved market (daily points for fidelity 1440 in the probe); the intel notes record that hourly and finer history needs startTs/endTs windows and that interval=max with fidelity 60 returned empty.
limitations: Probe covered one market; whether every earnings token has hourly history is the first coverage question of the build and is reported in data-feasibility.json; thin markets can have no print for days (stale flag).
impact_on_spec: Frozen definitions of P, P7 and the stale flag.

claim: Polymarket-v1 on Hugging Face (on-chain OrderFilled, CTF and daily_aligned tables) is licensed cc-by-4.0; it is a tick-level archive that is 27.4 GB for OrderFilled alone and was not chosen for this test.
limitations: Trade-level, covers to 2026-04 only, no order book; CLOB prices-history is simpler and point-in-time per request.
impact_on_spec: Recorded in data-feasibility.json as the fallback.

claim: Qin and Yang (arXiv 2606.04217) describe the Polymarket-v1 on-chain trade archive, 2022-11-21 to 2026-04-28, 1.20 billion trades, and show that tick-rule and bulk-volume classifiers are near random on it.
quote: We introduce the Polymarket-v1 Database: the complete on-chain trade archive
limitations: A data and microstructure paper with no stock-return test.
impact_on_spec: Stale-print rule and volume filter motivation.
